title: Predictability of El Ni\~no from Delayed Observations
abstract: arXiv:2608.24428v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Using monthly Ni\~no-3.4 anomalies through July 2026, we investigate how much predictive information is contained in delayed observations of the index. Ridge regression identifies informative delays, while multilayer perceptron and sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) models test whether nonlinear complexity provides additional direct forecast skill; gated recurrent unit (GRU) and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks provide a complementary test in which the temporal representation is learned internally. Delayed observations substantially improve forecasts over persistence and climatology at leads of up to six months, but increasing model complexity provides no systematic improvement. Historical recursive experiments favor a simple explicit SINDy recurrence and select shallow recurrent architectures, with no appreciable gain from learning the temporal representation internally. translated_title: 延迟观测对厄尔尼诺可预测性的研究
translated_abstract: 摘要：使用截至2026年7月的月度尼诺-3.4异常数据，我们研究了该指数延迟观测中包含多少预测信息。岭回归识别出信息丰富的延迟，而多层感知器和非线性动力学稀疏识别（SINDy）模型测试了非线性复杂性是否提供额外的直接预测技能；门控循环单元（GRU）和长短期记忆（LSTM）网络提供了互补测试，其中时间表示在内部学习。延迟观测在长达六个月的预测提前期内显著优于持续性和气候学预测，但增加模型复杂性并未带来系统性改进。历史递归实验倾向于简单的显式SINDy递归，并选择浅层递归架构，从内部学习时间表示没有明显收益。这些结果支持一个紧凑的预测框架。
tldr: 该研究通过比较多种模型发现，延迟观测数据能显著提升厄尔尼诺预测技能，但增加模型复杂性（如深度学习）并未带来系统性改进，支持使用简单的显式SINDy递归模型进行紧凑预测。
en_tdlr: This study finds that delayed observations significantly improve El Niño forecast skill, but increasing model complexity (e.g., deep learning) provides no systematic gain, favoring a simple explicit SINDy recurrence for compact prediction.
